rationale: Tests the learner's ability to apply indications for LSCS — a core decision point when observing the case
Anchors learning about intraoperative complications — specifically the risk moment in a previous-scar LSCS that observers should recognise
Tests knowledge of the ureteric danger zone — the most critical anatomical landmark the observer must identify during hysterectomy
Tests recognition of bladder injury during hysterectomy — a complication the observer should be able to spot and understand
Tests understanding of D&C sequencing — a key decision point observers must track step by step
Tests recognition of uterine perforation — the most important complication the observer must identify and understand its mechanism
Tests prerequisite criteria for outlet forceps — the conditions the observer must confirm are met before forceps are applied
Tests the critical Lovset's manoeuvre during breech delivery — a specific decision point observers must understand
Tests MTP Act 2021 key provisions — factual knowledge observers need to contextualise the consent and legal framework they see in theatre
Tests recognition of post-aspiration completeness check — a critical decision point the observer must interpret
Tests the observer's understanding of pneumoperitoneum entry technique and the consequence of wrong-plane insufflation — a high-stakes decision point at laparoscopy
Tests the key safety rule for laparoscopic sterilization — tracing the fallopian tube from the cornu before clip application
